headline: Forest’s chance volume outstrips Ipswich in 1–1 draw

sentences.text: Ipswich Town and Nottingham Forest shared the points in a 1–1 draw, but the underlying numbers tilted sharply toward the visitors.
Forest recorded 2.29 expected goals to Ipswich’s 0.46, alongside a 17–7 advantage in shots and 5–3 in attempts on target.
The visitors also created 2 big chances to Ipswich’s 1 and won 5 corners while Ipswich had none, though possession was nearly even at 50.6% to 49.4%.
Neco Williams put Forest ahead in the 13th minute, and Julio Enciso levelled for Ipswich in the 41st; neither side scored after the break.
Forest made the stronger threat without turning that advantage into a second goal, while the draw moved Ipswich to 9th on 10 points and Forest to 16th on 6.
Both sides entered with inconsistent recent league runs: Ipswich had taken 6 points from 5 matches, Forest 4 from 5.
